data.title: STI kits (NACO colour-coded kits)
data.summary: XI Miscellaneous · Pre-packed syndromic treatment kits supplied free under the National AIDS Control Programme (NACO) — 7 colour-coded kits
data.body:
_Oral · XI Miscellaneous_

**Class:** Pre-packed syndromic treatment kits supplied free under the National AIDS Control Programme (NACO) — 7 colour-coded kits

## Mechanism of action
- Syndromic case management: treats all the common organisms that cause a given syndrome at the first visit, without waiting for lab tests
- Each kit is a single complete course, which improves adherence; partners get the same kit

## Pharmacokinetics
- See each component drug (azithromycin, cefixime, secnidazole, fluconazole, benzathine penicillin, doxycycline, acyclovir, metronidazole)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Kit 1 — Grey: urethral discharge, anorectal discharge, cervicitis → azithromycin 1 g single dose + cefixime 400 mg single dose
- Kit 2 — Green: vaginal discharge (vaginitis: trichomonas, bacterial vaginosis, candida) → secnidazole 2 g single dose + fluconazole 150 mg single dose
- Kit 3 — White: genital ulcer disease, non-herpetic (syphilis, chancroid) → benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM single dose (with sterile water and syringe) + azithromycin 1 g single dose
- Kit 4 — Blue: genital ulcer disease, non-herpetic, for penicillin allergy → doxycycline 100 mg twice daily × 15 days + azithromycin 1 g single dose
- Kit 5 — Red: genital ulcer disease, herpetic → acyclovir 400 mg three times daily × 7 days
- Kit 6 — Yellow: lower abdominal pain (PID) → cefixime 400 mg single dose + metronidazole 400 mg twice daily × 14 days + doxycycline 100 mg twice daily × 14 days
- Kit 7 — Black: inguinal bubo (LGV, chancroid) → doxycycline 100 mg twice daily × 21 days + azithromycin 1 g single dose

## Dose & formulations
- Given as the full kit to the patient, with an identical kit (or appropriate treatment) for each partner
- Pregnancy: avoid doxycycline kits (blue, black, yellow) — use erythromycin/azithromycin alternatives as per NACO; secnidazole avoided in the first trimester

## Adverse effects
- As for the individual drugs: GI upset (azithromycin, metronidazole, doxycycline), disulfiram-like reaction (metronidazole/secnidazole with alcohol), Jarisch–Herxheimer reaction and anaphylaxis risk (benzathine penicillin), photosensitivity (doxycycline)

## Contraindications
- Kit 3 (white): penicillin allergy → use kit 4 (blue)
- Doxycycline kits in pregnancy, breastfeeding and children under 8
- Avoid alcohol with kits containing metronidazole or secnidazole

## Drug interactions
- See component drugs

## Monitoring
- Follow-up at 7 days (14 days for ulcers and PID) to check response
- Offer HIV and syphilis testing, condoms, partner notification and counselling (the '4 Cs': compliance, counselling, condoms, contact tracing)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Adjust in pregnancy (no doxycycline); syphilis in pregnancy → benzathine penicillin (desensitise if allergic).

## Viva points
- Know each colour and its contents — a favourite viva question
- Grey = urethral discharge; Green = vaginal discharge; White = non-herpetic ulcer; Blue = non-herpetic ulcer with penicillin allergy; Red = herpetic ulcer; Yellow = lower abdominal pain; Black = bubo
- Syndromic approach — treat the patient and partner at the first visit
- 4 Cs of STI management

## Note on sources
The kit contents follow NACO's standard 7-kit scheme. The exam list names 5 colours (white, green, blue, yellow, black), but all 7 are included because grey and red are commonly asked too. Please check against the latest NACO technical guidelines in case your hospital supply differs.

_Sources: NACO National Guidelines on Prevention, Management and Control of RTI including STI (colour-coded kits); not covered in Wolverton or Khopkar. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
